Honour
Above All.

For over 50 years, the Richmond Hill Budokan has trained students of every age in traditional Kitsune Ryu Jiu-Jitsu, OGKK Goju Ryu Karate, and Tai Chi & Qigong — building character, resilience, and community.

Our Philosophy

Our goal is to give students the opportunity to succeed in martial arts and in life — an inclusive space to learn, build confidence, and grow as part of a community, for students of all ages and abilities.

Students build character, resilience, and team spirit alongside technical skill — from their first class at age five through a lifetime of practice. It's the same standard O-Sensei Steve Reynolds set when he opened his dojo's doors in 1973, and the same one we hold today.

Programs

Three disciplines, one dojo.

柔

Kitsune Ryu Jiu-Jitsu

Founded 1973 · Modern Jujutsu

A modern (gendai) Jiu-Jitsu system founded by O-Sensei Steve Reynolds, drawing on Canadian Jiu-Jitsu, Kodenkan and Small Circle Jiu-Jitsu lineage. Training covers forms, weapons, and self-defense across ten original katas from white belt to black.

Learn more →
空

OGKK Goju Ryu Karate

Okinawan lineage · Traditional forms

Affiliated with the Okinawa Goju Ryu Karate-do Kyokai (OGKK) through the Canadian branch and Patrick Barton Sensei, our Karate program teaches traditional Okinawan forms, kata, and instruction graded by Okinawan Masters.

Learn more →
気

Tai Chi & Qigong

Yang style · White Crane practice

Incorporating Yang Style Tai Chi principles and White Crane Qigong practices, our wellness classes are built for longevity, mobility, and optimum health at any age.

Learn more →

Our Founder

O-Sensei Steve Reynolds

1948 — 2022

Read the full story →

A lifelong martial artist who began studying Kung Fu as a boy in Newfoundland, O-Sensei Reynolds trained across the Canadian military and NATO postings in West Germany before returning home to study under Prof. Ronald W. Forrester of the Canadian Jiu-Jitsu Association — building relationships with masters like Prof. Wally Jay and Hanshi Richard Kim along the way.

In October 1973, he opened his own dojo in Richmond Hill. Over fifty years later, it's still teaching his curriculum, his katas, and his motto: Honour Above All.

The Path

Ten katas. White belt to black.

Kitsune Ryu Jiu-Jitsu is built on original kata developed by O-Sensei Reynolds himself — ten one-man combat sequences carrying a student from their first class through first-degree black belt, with a second set reserved for black belts continuing their development.
